subject: math
title: Grade 3 Equations and Equivalence
seo_title: Grade 3 Equations and Equivalence Worksheets: Free Math with Answer Key (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Determine what needs to be added to or subtracted from addition and subtraction expressions to make them equivalent
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 math worksheets on equations and equivalence for the Ontario curriculum: the equal sign as a balance, missing numbers like □ + 25 = 60, making both sides equal, letters for unknowns and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key, great EQAO practice.
key_big: The equal sign means “is the same as”. Both sides of an equation must have the same value.
body_html:
The equal sign means “the same as”

An equation has an = sign. The = sign does not mean “the answer comes next”. It means both sides have the same value, like a pan balance that is level.

Find the missing number

A box □ or a letter like n stands for an unknown number. Use the inverse: subtraction undoes addition, and addition undoes subtraction. Then put your answer back in to check.

EquationDo thisAnswer
□ + 25 = 6060 − 2535
80 − □ = 3580 − 3545
□ − 15 = 4040 + 1555
n + 6 = 1414 − 6n = 8
Example

□ − 15 = 40

The box is the number you start with. Undo − 15 by adding: 40 + 15 = 55. Check: 55 − 15 = 40.

Answer: 55

Make both sides equal

When both sides have numbers, work out the side you know first. Then find what the other side needs.

Example

40 + 15 = 50 + □

The left side is 40 + 15 = 55. So 50 + □ = 55, and □ = 55 − 50 = 5. Or: 50 is 10 more than 40, so the box is 10 less than 15.

Answer: 5

Example

What must be added to 45 + 20 to make it equal to 50 + 30?

45 + 20 = 65 and 50 + 30 = 80. 80 − 65 = 15.

Answer: 15

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
40 + 15 = 50 + □, so □ = 5555 is the left side. 50 + □ = 55, so □ = 5
40 + 15 = 50 + □, so □ = 2550 is more than 40, so □ is less than 15: □ = 5
□ + 25 = 60, so □ = 85 (60 + 25)Use the inverse: 60 − 25 = 35
□ − 15 = 40, so □ = 25 (40 − 15)Undo − 15 by adding: 40 + 15 = 55
80 − 35 = 55 (smaller digit from larger)Regroup: 80 − 35 = 45
9 + 6 = 15 + 5 = 20Write two equations: 9 + 6 = 15, then 15 + 5 = 20

faq.q: What does the equal sign mean in Grade 3 math?
faq.a: The equal sign means “is the same as”, not “the answer is”. In 40 + 15 = 50 + □, both sides must have the same value, so the box is 5, not 55.

faq.q: How do you find the missing number in an equation like □ + 25 = 60?
faq.a: Use the inverse operation: subtraction undoes addition, so □ = 60 − 25 = 35. For □ − 15 = 40, add: 40 + 15 = 55. Then put the number back in to check.

faq.q: Why do Grade 3 students use letters like n in equations?
faq.a: The Ontario curriculum (Algebra C2.1) has Grade 3 students use symbols and letters for unknown numbers. A letter works just like a box: in n + 6 = 14, n = 8.

faq.q: Are equations and equivalence part of the Grade 3 EQAO math assessment?
faq.a: The Grade 3 EQAO math assessment is based on the Ontario curriculum, which includes the Algebra strand. Practising missing numbers, balances and word problems like these builds the skills students need.

items.e: The pans balance, so both sides have the same value. The left pan has 7 + 5 and the right pan has 12, so 7 + 5 = 12. The = sign can sit between any two things that are the same.

items.q:
□ = 8 + 7
What number goes in the box?
items.e: The = sign can come first. The box is the same as 8 + 7, so it is 15. Not 1: that subtracts.

items.q:
□ = 30 − 12
What number goes in the box?
items.e: The box is the same as 30 − 12. 30 − 12 = 18. Not 42: that adds. Not 22: that takes 0 from 2 instead of regrouping.

items.q: What does the = sign mean in 6 + 4 = 7 + 3?
items.e: = means “is the same as”. 6 + 4 = 10 and 7 + 3 = 10, so both sides are the same. It does not just mean “the answer comes next”.

items.q: Benjamin adds 9 and 6, then adds 5. He writes 9 + 6 = 15 + 5 = 20. What is wrong?
items.e: = means both sides are the same. 9 + 6 = 15, but 15 + 5 = 20, so “9 + 6 = 15 + 5” is not true. Benjamin should write two equations: 9 + 6 = 15 and 15 + 5 = 20.

items.q:
The pans balance: 40 + 15 = 50 + □.
What number goes in the box?
items.e: Both sides must have the same value. The left side is 40 + 15 = 55. So 50 + □ = 55 and □ = 5. Or: 50 is 10 more than 40, so □ must be 10 less than 15. Not 55: that is the value of the left side, not the missing number. Not 25: that changes 15 the wrong way.

What number goes in the box?

items.q:
□ + 20 = 18 + 25
What number goes in the box?

□ + 29 = 34 + 25
What number goes in the box?

items.q:
The pans balance: 45 − 15 = 50 − □.
What number goes in the box?

items.q:
What number must be added to 45 + 20 to make both sides equal?
45 + 20 + □ = 50 + 30
items.e: The right side is 50 + 30 = 80. The left side has 45 + 20 = 65. 80 − 65 = 15, so add 15. Not 80: that is the right side. Not 5: that only compares 45 and 50.

items.q:
What number must be added to 36 + 14 to make both sides equal?
36 + 14 + □ = 40 + 25
items.e: The right side is 40 + 25 = 65. The left side has 36 + 14 = 50. 65 − 50 = 15, so add 15. Not 65: that is the right side. Not 4: that only compares 36 and 40.

items.q:
What number must be subtracted from 60 + 25 to make both sides equal?
60 + 25 − □ = 70
items.e: 60 + 25 = 85. To get from 85 down to 70, subtract 85 − 70 = 15. Not 85: that is the left side. Not 10: that only compares 60 and 70.

items.q:
What number must be subtracted from 90 − 30 to make both sides equal?
90 − 30 − □ = 50
items.e: 90 − 30 = 60. To get from 60 down to 50, subtract 60 − 50 = 10. Not 60: that is 90 − 30. Not 40: that is 90 − 50 and forgets the − 30.

items.q: n + 6 = 14. What is n?
items.e: The letter n stands for the unknown number. Use the inverse: n = 14 − 6 = 8. Check: 8 + 6 = 14. Not 20: that adds instead of subtracting.

items.q: a − 12 = 30. What is a?
items.e: a is the number you start with. Undo − 12 by adding: a = 30 + 12 = 42. Check: 42 − 12 = 30. Not 18: that subtracts instead of adding.

items.q: b − 45 = 27. What is b?
items.e: b is the number you start with. Undo − 45 by adding: b = 27 + 45 = 72. Check: 72 − 45 = 27. Not 18: that subtracts instead of adding.

items.q: The pans balance: x + 15 = 15 + 20. What is x?
items.e: You can add in any order: 20 + 15 = 15 + 20. So x = 20. Not 35: that is the value of the right side.

items.q: The pans balance: h + 30 = 40 + 25. What is h?
items.e: The right side is 40 + 25 = 65. So h + 30 = 65 and h = 65 − 30 = 35. Not 65: that is the right side. Not 15: 30 is less than 40, so h must be more than 25, not less.

items.q: Which equation means the same as □ + 9 = 21?
items.e: A letter can take the place of the box. Both stand for the same unknown number: k + 9 = 21. In both, the unknown is 12.

items.q: Which equation is true when a = 7?
items.e: Put 7 in place of a. 7 + 8 = 15, so a + 8 = 15 is true.

items.q: Which equation is true when n = 25?
items.e: Put 25 in place of n. 25 + 25 = 50, so n + 25 = 50 is true.

items.q: Which equation means “a number plus 12 is 30”?
items.e: Let n be the number. “Plus 12” is + 12 and “is 30” is = 30: n + 12 = 30. Then n = 18.

items.q: Which equation means “a number take away 8 is 25”?
items.e: Start with the number n, take away 8, and get 25: n − 8 = 25. Then n = 25 + 8 = 33. 8 − n starts with 8, not with the number.

items.q: What is n in the bar model?
items.e: The two parts make the whole: 45 + n = 70. So n = 70 − 45 = 25. Not 115: that adds. Not 35: that takes the smaller digit from the larger.

items.q: What is m in the bar model?
items.e: m is the whole, so add the parts: 36 + 48 = 84. Not 12: that subtracts. Not 74: that forgets to carry the ten from 6 + 8 = 14.

items.q: Maya solves y + 17 = 40 and gets y = 57. What did she do wrong?
items.e: 57 + 17 is 74, not 40. She added instead of subtracting. Use the inverse: y = 40 − 17 = 23. Check: 23 + 17 = 40.

items.q: Sofia has 25 hockey cards. She gets some more. Now she has 60. Which equation shows this?
items.e: Sofia starts with 25, gets an unknown number more and ends with 60: 25 + □ = 60. Then □ = 60 − 25 = 35.

items.q: Hana picks 37 apples at the orchard. She wants 80 apples. How many more does she need to pick?
items.e: Equation: 37 + □ = 80. Use the inverse: □ = 80 − 37 = 43 apples. Check: 37 + 43 = 80. Not 117: that adds.

items.q: A Grade 3 class has raised $85 for the Terry Fox Run. The goal is $150. How much more do they need to raise?
items.e: Equation: 85 + □ = 150. □ = 150 − 85 = $65. Check: $85 + $65 = $150. Not $235: that adds instead of subtracting.

items.q: There were 80 Canada geese on a pond. Some flew away. Now 35 are left. How many flew away?
items.e: Equation: 80 − □ = 35. □ = 80 − 35 = 45 geese. Check: 80 − 45 = 35. Not 115: that adds. Not 55: that takes 0 from 5 instead of regrouping.

items.q: A bus takes students to the skating rink. At the first stop, 18 students get off. Now 24 are on the bus. Let s be the number of students at the start. Which equation matches?
items.e: Start with s, 18 get off, and 24 are left: s − 18 = 24. Then s = 24 + 18 = 42.

items.q: A bus takes students to the skating rink. At the first stop, 18 students get off. Now 24 are on the bus. How many students were on the bus at the start?
items.e: Equation: s − 18 = 24. Undo − 18 by adding: s = 24 + 18 = 42 students. Check: 42 − 18 = 24. Not 6: that subtracts instead of adding. Not 32: that forgets to carry the ten.

items.q: The school library has 500 books in the reading corner. 275 are in English and the rest are in French. How many books are in French?
A sugar shack makes 400 L of maple syrup in March. It makes 150 L in the first week. How many litres does it make in the rest of March?
Olivia has 30 red blocks and 20 blue blocks. Ethan has 40 red blocks. Ethan wants the same number of blocks as Olivia. Which equation shows how many blue blocks Ethan needs?
items.e: The two totals must be the same, so the two sides are equal: 30 + 20 = 40 + □. 30 + 20 = 50, so □ = 10 blue blocks.

items.q: Owen has 26 stickers and gets 8 more. Lucas has 30 stickers. How many more does Lucas need to have the same number as Owen?
items.e: Equation: 26 + 8 = 30 + □. 26 + 8 = 34. So 30 + □ = 34 and □ = 4. Not 34: that is Owen’s total. Not 12: 30 is more than 26, so Lucas needs fewer than 8, not more.

items.q: Leah’s family goes on a 120 km canoe trip. They paddle 45 km on day 1 and 40 km on day 3. How far do they paddle on day 2?
items.e: Equation: 45 + □ + 40 = 120. 45 + 40 = 85. So 85 + □ = 120 and □ = 120 − 85 = 35 km. Not 75: that forgets the 40 km on day 3. Not 205: that adds all the numbers.

items.q: Liam reads p pages on Saturday and 35 pages on Sunday. He reads 90 pages in all. Which equation matches?
items.e: Saturday’s pages plus Sunday’s pages make 90: p + 35 = 90. Then p = 90 − 35 = 55.

items.q: Liam reads p pages on Saturday and 35 pages on Sunday. He reads 90 pages in all. How many pages did he read on Saturday?
items.e: Equation: p + 35 = 90. p = 90 − 35 = 55 pages. Check: 55 + 35 = 90. Not 125: that adds.

items.q: A school has 600 students. On a snow day, only 245 students come to school. How many students stay home?
items.e: Equation: 245 + □ = 600. □ = 600 − 245 = 355 students. Check: 245 + 355 = 600. Not 845: that adds. Not 445: that takes the smaller digit from the larger instead of regrouping.

items.q: Emma works out 72 − 38 = 34. Which equation can she use to check her answer?
items.e: Check a subtraction with addition, the inverse: 34 + 38 = 72 is true, so the answer is right. 72 + 38 = 110 is true too, but it does not check the subtraction.

items.q: Kai has some money. He spends $15 at the fall fair and has $28 left. How much money did he have at the start?
items.e: Equation: □ − 15 = 28. Undo − 15 by adding: □ = 28 + 15 = $43. Check: $43 − $15 = $28. Not $13: that subtracts. Not $33: that forgets to carry the ten.

items.q: There are 28 students in gym class. 13 are on the red team and the rest are on the blue team. How many are on the blue team?
items.e: Equation: 13 + □ = 28. □ = 28 − 13 = 15 students. Check: 13 + 15 = 28. Not 41: that adds.

items.q: Aiden’s family needs 64 buns for Thanksgiving dinner. They have 38 buns. Let b be the number of buns they still need. Which equation matches?
items.e: They have 38, they need b more, and that makes 64: 38 + b = 64. Then b = 64 − 38 = 26.

items.q: The school wants to collect 1000 cans for the food bank. So far it has 640 cans. How many more cans does it need?
Jayden’s family drives 450 km to the cottage. They stop for lunch after 280 km. Which equation shows how far they still have to drive?
items.e: They drove 280 km, they still have □ km, and the whole trip is 450 km: 280 + □ = 450. Then □ = 450 − 280 = 170 km.
